summary.headline: Kalyani Cast-Tech guides FY27 order book rising to ~INR170 crore from INR133 crore, with H1 expected to lag and H2 to catch up.
summary.overview: Management presented FY26 results showing revenue up about 7.7%, PAT up about 20% and EPS up about 20% year on year. The company cited an order book of about INR133 crore, of which roughly 50% is innovative containers and INR45 crore is from government customers, and said it expects this to reach about INR170 crore soon. H1 FY27 was described as not going to plan due to war-related supply chain disruption, with management saying H2 would catch up. Capacity additions included a second Shivlakha (Kutch, Gujarat) container line, a rail-connected Gati Shakti cargo terminal, ICD permission and a wagon plant awaiting RDSO audit.

financial_highlights.value: None drawn; INR100 crore HDFC Bank sanction available

segments.name: Container manufacturing (Rewari, Haryana)
segments.commentary: Capacity ~7,000 TEU, FY26 output ~5,400 TEU, utilisation ~75-80%. Management guides container PAT margin ~10-11%.

segments.name: Container manufacturing (Shivlakha, Kutch)
segments.commentary: Capacity ~10,000 TEU per year, production started June 2026 with 500 containers delivered; plant has surplus capacity. Overall capacity cited as ~17,000 TEU.

segments.name: Wagon manufacturing
segments.commentary: Phase-one capacity 2,400 wagons per year; factory complete but awaiting RDSO G-105 audit. Design stage-1 cleared; 60-70% of wagon cost is bought-out items, so value addition is limited.

segments.name: ICD and rail terminal
segments.commentary: ICD permission received 10 Sept 2026, warehouse foundation laid 14 Sept, operations expected by next financial year. Management guides EBITDA margin ~25-30% for ICD and terminal operations.

guidance_outlook: Order book expected to rise from ~INR133 crore to ~INR170 crore; management said this would be the FY27 revenue guidance, though the analyst was not clear on whether it referred to order book or top line.
H1 FY27 expected to be weaker than planned due to supply chain disruption from war; management expects H2 catch-up but gave no H1 figure.
Long-term vision cited as INR2,000-4,000 crore (or INR4,500 crore over 5-6 years in one answer); wagons at ~2,000 units per year alone would exceed INR1,000 crore.
Container capacity to be expanded from ~17,000 to ~25,000 TEU to qualify for the INR10,000 crore government container scheme; guidelines still awaited.
Expected capex for 1 lakh TEU greenfield at Kutch: INR1,400 crore; new foundry INR80-90 crore, likely next financial year.
capex_capacity: Rewari container plant ~7,000 TEU capacity, FY26 output ~5,400 TEU.
Shivlakha integrated facility: ~10,000 TEU container capacity (production since June 2026) plus wagon capacity ~2,400 per year.
Two full-length railway lines at Shivlakha inaugurated by Railway Minister on 15 Sept 2026; container handling equipment currently on hire.
Land of ~144 acres (possibly 150) at Kutch; ~60 acres kept for a large factory with offtake partner.
Capex funded from internal accruals and promoter warrants so far; management says debt and preferential issue/rights issue are under consideration for the next expansion.
demand_pricing: Order book ~INR133 crore, about 50% innovative containers (dwarf open-top, stainless steel, foldable, wide 20-ft with roof hatches, super high-cube 40-ft, two-wheeler triple-deck) and 50% standard containers.

Customers cited include JSW Ports (~1,500 containers this year), Western Carrier (50 foldable containers), Central Warehousing Corporation and Indian Navy (new, ~INR30 crore orders), Container Corporation via business associates, Pristine Logistics, Amba Coach Builders, Rail Connect and HTPL.
Pricing not disclosed; management declined to give average price of innovative containers.
Management said India's domestic container market is cyclical and that China supplies ~95-97% of global containers; the company claims ~60% share of Indian domestic container manufacturing.
Briskworld Ventures receivable of ~INR4.67 crore (per annual report) is now being paid, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How much will the new Kutch facility add to FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management restated the INR170 crore figure, which it described as the order book target, and did not give a separate top-line number.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company benefit from the INR10,000 crore container manufacturing scheme, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidelines are awaited (2-4 months expected). Company would need 25,000 TEU capacity to qualify as brownfield; currently ~17,000 TEU.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company have enough capital and what are the EBIT/PAT margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion to ~20,000 TEU more needs significant capex; options are bank debt (HDFC INR100 crore sanction), preferential issue or rights issue. Container PAT margin ~10-11%; ICD/terminal EBITDA ~25-30%.

qa_highlights.question: When will the RDSO wagon approval come and what is the stage-2 timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage-2 documentation to be submitted in 1-2 weeks; then prototype and oscillation trials. Final approval targeted by 31 March 2027. G-105 is a separate factory audit still pending; no inspection expected before Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any MOU, patent or equity interest from customers?
qa_highlights.answer: The MOU is with RDSO for joint design development. Management said the design is company-controlled. No customer or institution has shown interest in equity; management said it may not pursue such tie-ups.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for a new foundry and when?
qa_highlights.answer: New foundry (INR80-90 crore) to come in the next financial year, after wagon orders are confirmed. A small corner-casting foundry exists at Rewari.

risks_watch: H1 FY27 shortfall due to supply chain disruption; no H1 numbers disclosed and management deferred to the half-yearly balance sheet.
Dependence on RDSO audit and design approval for wagon revenue; timelines are management-controlled but not third-party confirmed.
Funding: capex for ~20,000 TEU more and ICD could require debt or dilutive equity; management says it is currently debt-free.
Government scheme eligibility and guidelines pending; CONCOR and CWC tendering can lead to abnormally low bids and non-supply, per management.
Limited disclosure: management declined to share pricing, H1 figures and the order book breakdown in detail; the INR133 crore vs INR135 crore figure was inconsistent in the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term vision and innovation, but cautious and evasive on near-term numbers: H1 figures, pricing, FY27 top line and timelines for government approvals were deferred or not given.

So, basically, margins in the container activity will remain around 10% to 11% PAT I'm telling, not that big a PAT.
Naresh Kumar: Right now we have not yet decided. We will go by the statutory requirement.
So basically, as we have been telling that these wagons can carry 42-foot containers on the chassis.

adds.what: Second Shivlakha (Kutch) container line, ~10,000 TEU/yr, production started June 2026
Gati Shakti rail-connected cargo terminal / ICD at Shivlakha, operations expected by next financial year
Wagon plant phase-one, 2,400 wagons/yr, factory complete awaiting RDSO G-105 audit

growth.why: Management expects order book to rise from ~INR133 cr to ~INR170 cr (about 28% implied), backed by a commissioned second Shivlakha line and a wagon plant awaiting audit, but H1 FY27 is weak due to war-related supply disruption and no H1 figure was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides container PAT margin at ~10-11% and ICD/terminal EBITDA at ~25-30%, but gave no consolidated margin path and H1 is weak from war-related supply disruption.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Second Shivlakha line (~10,000 TEU/yr) started production June 2026 with 500 containers delivered, taking overall capacity to ~17,000 TEU; ICD ops expected by next financial year.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book guided to rise from ~INR133 crore to ~INR170 crore (~28% implied), and Rewari utilisation is ~75-80% against ~5,400 TEU FY26 output, but H1 FY27 is expected to lag with no figure given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Rewari utilisation at ~77.5% and management says at least another 20,000 TEU is needed, with a INR1,400 crore 1 lakh TEU Kutch greenfield and INR80-90 crore foundry planned for next financial year.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 FY27 is weaker than planned from war-related supply disruption and management gave no H1 figure, so no upgrade signal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management admits H1 is not going to plan due to supply chain disruption, RDSO G-105 audit is still pending with no inspection before Diwali, and the INR170 crore target is ambiguous between order book and revenue.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Innovative containers are ~50% of the ~INR133 crore order book (dwarf open-top, stainless steel, foldable, super high-cube 40-ft, two-wheeler triple-deck), and wagon phase-one (2,400/yr) awaits RDSO stage-2 approval targeted by 31 March 2027.

rows.label: RDSO wagon approval (stage-2 and G-105 audit)
rows.why: Stage-2 documents due in 1-2 weeks, final approval targeted by 31 March 2027, but G-105 factory audit still pending with no inspection expected before Diwali.

rows.label: INR10,000 crore government container scheme eligibility
rows.why: Guidelines awaited (2-4 months expected); company needs 25,000 TEU to qualify as brownfield versus ~17,000 TEU today, so eligibility requires further expansion.

rows.label: Funding of next expansion (debt or dilutive equity)
rows.why: Company is debt-free with INR100 crore HDFC sanction undrawn, but ~20,000 TEU more capex plus ICD need debt, preferential or rights issue, which management says are under consideration.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term vision, Kutch capacity and innovative containers, but cautious and evasive on H1 numbers, pricing, FY27 top line and government approval timing; analysts pushed on whether INR170 crore is order book or revenue.
